case_title.quote: STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH v. SURENDRA KORI
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption.

number_of_accused.correct_value: Multiple: respondent plus vendees, vendors, witnesses and deed writer named in the charge-sheet
number_of_accused.quote: against the respondent and also against persons who got the sale deeds executed
number_of_accused.reason: Only the respondent is the appellant's target, but the charge-sheet names several other accused persons.

accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to with male pronouns throughout.

accused_age.reason: The judgment nowhere states the respondent's age.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.quote: Amar Singh s/o Chandar Singh Caste- Rajput, r/o Bamhnala
accused_caste.reason: Rajput is the caste of the vendor Amar Singh, not the respondent accused.

accused_occupation.quote: the respondent herein, who was functioning as the Deputy Registrar, Khargone
accused_occupation.reason: Judgment states respondent was Deputy Registrar.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Socioeconomic status is not stated in the judgment.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No previous criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.reason: No individual victim is identified; victims are the State and oustees.

offence_category.correct_value: Cheating, forgery and criminal conspiracy (IPC ss.420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B; Registration Act)
offence_category.quote: offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 read with Sections 34 and 1208 of the Indian Penal Code
offence_category.reason: Criminal breach of trust is never mentioned; charges are cheating, forgery, use of forged documents and conspiracy.

statutory_provisions.quote: 420, 467, 468, 469, 471 read with Sections 34 and 120-B of the IPC
statutory_provisions.reason: Value omits IPC s.469, which appears in the charge-sheet; other listed sections are supported.

weapon.reason: No weapon is mentioned in the judgment.

evidence_type.correct_value: Documentary evidence (sale deeds, enquiry and inspection reports); handwriting and thumb-impression comparison pending
evidence_type.quote: the certified hand writing examination report and the necessary documents and the statement of the district registrar are to be taken
evidence_type.reason: No medical evidence or recovery is mentioned; judgment describes documentary and pending forensic evidence.

confession.reason: No confession by the accused is mentioned.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Magnitude of crime; more than 102 fraudulent sale deeds; loss to State exchequer
aggravating_circumstances.quote: in view of the magnitude of the crime, the number of documents alleged to have been executed fraudulently
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Judgment expressly identifies magnitude of crime and number of fraudulent deeds as relevant factors.

trial_court_outcome.quote: a final report (charge-sheet No. 546 of 2007) was submitted under Section 173(8) Cr.P.C. before the Court
trial_court_outcome.reason: Charge-sheet filed; no trial outcome has been reached.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: High Court quashed FIRs, charge-sheets and criminal cases under s.482 CrPC
high_court_outcome.quote: in exercise of its powers under Section 482 CrPC quashed the First Information Reports and the charge-sheets
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court did act; it quashed the FIRs and charge-sheets, so 'Not applicable' is wrong.

final_outcome.correct_value: Supreme Court allowed the State's appeals and set aside the High Court judgments; no conviction
final_outcome.quote: The criminal appeals are accordingly allowed and the judgments of the High Court are set aside.
final_outcome.reason: Respondent was never convicted; the matter goes back to trial with prima facie observations only.

offence_finally_established.correct_value: None established; only prima facie allegations for trial
offence_finally_established.quote: We make it clear that whatever we have stated above are only prima facie observations
offence_finally_established.reason: No offence was finally established; the court expressly limited its observations to prima facie views.

imprisonment_type.reason: No sentence was imposed; the judgment only quashes or restores proceedings.

imprisonment_years.quote: shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years
imprisonment_years.reason: Seven years is the maximum punishment under s.81, not a sentence imposed on the respondent.

fine_rs.reason: No fine was imposed, so null is consistent with the judgment.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Neutral summary of facts without outcome; the accused was charged with cheating, forgery and conspiracy, not breach of trust
neutral_facts.quote: the Supreme Court overturned this decision, stating that the High Court should not have quashed the proceedings
neutral_facts.reason: Summary reveals the court outcome and wrongly states breach of trust was charged.

offence_severity.quote: shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both
offence_severity.reason: Matches the penalty stated for s.81 of the Registration Act.

attempt_completion.quote: more than 102 sale deeds relating to the same transaction were executed
attempt_completion.reason: Judgment states the sale deeds were executed and registered.

number_of_offences.quote: more than 102 sale deeds relating to the same transaction were executed
number_of_offences.reason: Supported by the judgment's statement on the number of deeds.

financial_property_loss.quote: putting the government in financial loss of Rs.339857/-
financial_property_loss.reason: Loss figure of Rs.3,39,857 is stated in the FIR and charge-sheet.

premeditation_planning.quote: the respondent has also conspired and abetted the crime
premeditation_planning.reason: Judgment records the allegation of conspiracy and abetment.

motive.quote: the forged sale deeds were executed for unlawful gain
motive.reason: Unlawful gain is the stated motive.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Prima facie allegations only; the court did not accept the evidence and left involvement to be decided at trial
key_evidence_accepted.quote: the question of involvement of respondent has to be finally decided depending upon the evidence in the case
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court only noted prima facie allegations and did not accept evidence as proving involvement.

witness_credibility.quote: The allegations raised in the charge-sheets are prima facie allegations and the question of involvement of respondent has to be finally decided depending upon the evidence
witness_credibility.reason: The judgment assesses no witness credibility; that is left to the trial.

post_offence_conduct.quote: The respondent was suspended from the service
post_offence_conduct.reason: Suspension is administrative action, not stated as post-offence conduct; no conduct is otherwise described.

custody_duration.reason: Duration of custody is not stated.

trial_duration.reason: Offence period, High Court judgment date and Supreme Court date are stated, not 'Not stated'.

legal_representation.correct_value: {"accused": "Ardhendumauli Kumar Prasad", "state": "Sidharth Dave, Abhimanyu Singh, C.D. Singh"}
legal_representation.quote: Sidharth Dave, Abhimanyu Singh, C.D. Singh for the Appellant. Ardhendumauli Kumar Prasad for the Respondent.
legal_representation.reason: Counsel assignments are swapped: Dave and others appeared for the State.

investigation_status.quote: investigation is still going on, after finishing which the full charge sheet will be submitted separately
investigation_status.reason: Charge-sheet filed and investigation continuing is stated.

procedural_irregularity.quote: the provisions of Section 64 of the Registration Act was not followed
procedural_irregularity.reason: Identity verification, s.64 non-compliance and missing PAN numbers are all supported.

appeal_history.correct_value: {"trial_court": "Not stated", "high_court": "High Court quashed FIRs and charge-sheets under s.482 CrPC", "supreme_court": "Supreme Court allowed appeals and set aside High Court judgments"}
appeal_history.quote: the judgments of the High Court are set aside
appeal_history.reason: High Court entry wrongly says it set aside judgments; it was the Supreme Court that did so.

prosecution_argument.quote: the Registrar is also instrumental in aiding the execution of several sale deeds by fictitious persons
prosecution_argument.reason: Summary matches State's arguments on instrumentality, loss and need for evidence.

defence_argument.quote: the respondent, in the capacity of the Sub-Registrar ... was bound to register the documents
defence_argument.reason: Defence argument on registration duty and lack of knowledge is accurately summarised.

legal_principle_applied.quote: inherent jurisdiction under the section though wide has to be exercised sparingly, carefully and with caution
legal_principle_applied.reason: Principle of sparing use of s.482 is stated in the judgment.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: M.M.T.C. Ltd.; State of Orissa v. Saroj Kumar Sahoo; Eicher Tractors v. Harihar Singh (relied on); Jambu Prasad (referred to only)
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Jambu Prasad v. Mohammad Nawab Aftab Ali Khan AIR 1941 PC 16 referred to
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Jambu Prasad was only referred to, not relied upon, and the value lists it as relied upon.

sentencing_rationale.reason: No sentence was imposed, so 'Not applicable' is consistent.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: No mitigating factors are identified by the court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Magnitude of crime; number of fraudulently executed documents; respondent's involvement
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: in view of the magnitude of the crime, the number of documents alleged to have been executed fraudulently, the reports referred to in the charge-sheets and the involvement of the respondent
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court expressly lists magnitude, number of documents and involvement as reasons for proceeding.

other_sentence_order.reason: No other sentence order is made; appeals allowed and HC judgments set aside.
